concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: A way of stating that a function grows no faster than a constant multiple of another function, beyond some input size.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers of the form a + bi with real a and b and imaginary unit i, with the usual addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Finite sums of constant multiples of powers of a variable, with coefficients drawn from a number system.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: An abstract machine with a finite control and a fixed number of tapes, each with its own head that reads and writes one cell per step.

concepts.name: Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: The conjecture of Schönhage and Strassen that n log n is the optimal order of growth of the cost of multiplying two n-bit integers on a multitape Turing machine.

evidence.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth

concepts.name: Exact integer multiplication
concepts.gloss: The task of computing the exact 2n-bit binary representation of the product of two n-bit binary integers given as input.

concepts.name: Fixed-tape machine model
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, where a step moves each head by at most one cell.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.

concepts.gloss: Complex numbers z with z^m = 1 for some positive integer m, whose powers cycle through a finite set.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The linear map that sends a sequence of n complex numbers to its values at the n-th roots of unity, weighted by powers of a root of unity.

concepts.name: Subset-intersection network

concepts.name: Fast address interchange
concepts.gloss: A tape procedure that swaps two equal-width address fields in an array by computing XOR combinations of intermediate data, at cost proportional to the volume times a power of the field width.

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields

concepts.name: Rank-saving recursion
concepts.gloss: The recursive construction in which the number of smaller calls is less than the wire count times the parameter, which gives a strict power saving in each level of the recursion.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.gloss: A single tape procedure that applies the two-point butterfly to the same selected bit position in several equal-width address chunks at once, at cost sublinear in the number of chunks.

evidence.quote: We now apply the complex network to a common butterfly layer on several axes

concepts.name: Exact recovery by rounding
concepts.gloss: The step that rounds the approximate convolution coefficients to integers, after the known normalizations are removed, and shows that each error is below one half.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$

concepts.gloss: A deterministic fixed-tape multitape Turing machine that multiplies two n-bit integers exactly in O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)) time with kappa = 2^(-182), which disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.
